study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Kim et al., Biological Psychiatry: Global Open Science, 2025
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Predicting Mental and Neurological Illnesses Based on Cerebellar Normative Features

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Clinical datasets for patients (AD, ASD, BD, MCI, SZ) and their matched healthy controls were obtained from ABIDE I and II, ADNI, AIBL, DEMGEN, and TOP (including StrokeMRI). The normative model was built using a large reference sample (N=54,102) from the same pool as the cerebellar lifespan normative model described in Kim et al. (2024), which likely includes multiple unspecified datasets for the neurotypical population.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: The clinical datasets were obtained from the ABIDE I and II (Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange I and II), ADNI (Alzheimer ' s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative), AIBL (The Australian Imaging, Biomarkers and Lifestyle Flagship Study), DEMGEN (Norwegian Dementia Genetics Network), and TOP (Thematically Organized Psychosis) cohorts... The study sample consisted of individuals from the cerebellar lifespan normative model (15), where individuals without a diagnosis were split into a training set ( n = 27,117; 54% female), a test set ( n = 26,985; 53% females), and a clinical set ( n = 1757; 30% females)
